topic: Municipalities / Urban Local Bodies of Indian Polity
description: The 74th Constitutional Amendment Act of 1992 granted constitutional status to Urban Local Bodies (Municipalities) in India. This forms a crucial part of democratic decentralization, strengthening urban administration and governance at the grassroots level.

sections.title: Historical Background
sections.description: The evolution of Urban Local Governance in India and its historical milestones.

historical_events.significance: It was the first Municipal Corporation in India, established during British rule to manage local civic affairs.

historical_events.event: Municipal Corporations in Bombay and Calcutta
historical_events.significance: Following Madras, municipal corporations were set up in the major presidency towns of Bombay and Calcutta.
Historically hailed as the 'Magna Carta of Local Self-Government', it laid the foundation for democratic local institutions in India.

important_facts.fact: Lord Ripon is universally recognized as the 'Father of Local Self-Government in India'.

sections.title: 74th Constitutional Amendment Act
sections.description: The landmark amendment that institutionalized Municipalities in the Constitution of India.

polity_articles.provision: Addition of Part IX-A and 12th Schedule
polity_articles.details: Added a new Part IX-A to the Constitution (Articles 243P to 243ZG) and the 12th Schedule, which enumerates 18 functional items for municipalities.

key_concepts.explanation: Constituted for a 'transitional area', meaning an area that is in the process of transitioning from a rural area to an urban area.
Constituted for 'smaller urban areas', managing the civic administration of towns and smaller cities.
The apex urban local body constituted for 'larger urban areas' or major metropolitan cities.

sections.title: Important Constitutional Articles (Part IX-A)
sections.description: Crucial articles governing the structure, elections, and functions of Municipalities (Articles 243P to 243ZG).

polity_articles.details: Mandates the creation of a Nagar Panchayat, a Municipal Council, or a Municipal Corporation in every State, based on the area's classification.
Provides reservation for SCs/STs in proportion to their population and mandates a minimum 1/3rd reservation of total seats for women.
Sets a fixed tenure of 5 years. In case of dissolution before the term ends, fresh elections must be held within 6 months.
Empowers the State Legislature to endow municipalities with powers and responsibilities, specifically regarding the 18 items listed in the 12th Schedule.
Mandates the constitution of a DPC to consolidate the plans prepared by both Panchayats and Municipalities in the district into a draft development plan.
Mandates the creation of an MPC to prepare a draft development plan for a Metropolitan area (an area having a population of 10 lakhs or more).

sections.title: Other Types of Urban Local Bodies
sections.description: Specific urban administrative structures that exist outside the standard municipal corporation or council framework.

key_concepts.explanation: Established for municipal administration of the civilian population in military areas. It functions directly under the administrative control of the Union Ministry of Defence and is governed by the Cantonments Act, 2006.

Created for the administration of newly developing towns or fast-growing industrial areas that do not yet meet all the conditions required for the constitution of a municipality. It is established via a government gazette notification.
Established by an Act of Parliament in major port areas (like Mumbai, Kolkata, Chennai) to manage and protect the ports while providing civic amenities to the port personnel.
Established by large public enterprises (PSUs) to provide civic amenities to their staff and workers who live in the housing colonies built near the plant or factory.

sections.title: Exam-Oriented Important Facts
sections.description: High-yield one-liner facts regarding urban local bodies frequently asked in competitive exams.

important_facts.fact: Urban Local Government is a subject under the 'State List' as per the 7th Schedule of the Indian Constitution.
The 12th Schedule of the Constitution contains a total of 18 functional items (subjects) such as urban planning, public health, and fire services.
The formal/ceremonial head of a Municipal Corporation is the 'Mayor', whereas the real executive and administrative powers are vested in the 'Municipal Commissioner' (typically an IAS officer).

The State Election Commission (instituted under Articles 243K and 243ZA) is solely responsible for the superintendence, direction, and control of the preparation of electoral rolls and conducting free and fair elections for all Municipalities.
